sections.title: What we're building
sections.text: Were designing a cozy isometric snowball fight game.  There are two teams, each team, has 4 players.  This is a single player game so I'm leaving it vague for you to decide.

sections.title: Decided (Foreman; host's calls outrank everything)
sections.text:
- 1 human + 3 AI allies (Pip, Scoop, Waffle) vs 4 AI. Match = first to 2 rounds of 120s (host): your hill, their hill, the park only at 1-1.
- Round: most crown-seconds with the toboggan. Sled starts beside the human in round 1, foot-centre in rounds 2–3. Every crown = same flat saddle. Tie → sudden death, capped 60s.
- Clock: afternoon → dusk (≥4 steps) → streetlights at 120s, plus a 20s countdown. Lighting resets each round.
- Camera: one fixed iso shot of the whole ~26m hill, kids ~48px at 720p. No pan.
- Controls (host): mouse only. Right-click walks to the cursor, left-click throws (hands off while carrying), middle-click builds.
- No elimination: a chilled kid warms up at the cocoa stand, ~8s, out of play. Target ≤2 chills per kid per round (bench + siege combined, <15%).
- Garage shop (host, rule 4): 4 credits/round guaranteed + hits + crown time; one purchase per visit; ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Upgrades and credits last the whole snow day (host), bots too; 'New snow day' wipes them with a porch-screen notice. Not yet built: bazooka, igloo, fort.
- Plain snowball = fast flat line, never clears a wall. Wall: one per kid, 1s plant at your feet, 8s cooldown (ghost footprint). Nothing built on the crown.
- Hits: first kid touched below head height in flight, or anyone in the ring at touchdown. One hit chills. No friendly fire.
- AI: Beanie, Pockets (blower), Brick (never throws), Copycat; fair-bot dodging.
- SIEGE: the crown holder faces one shared volley, ONE release frame per cadence, ≤4 live rings. Defenders 8m+ bracket the carrier's path; closer ones throw one direct shot. Cadence 2.0 / 1.5 / 1.45s per street; street 3 adds a second blower.
- FROSTY (host): bonus bout on 'Next street' / 'New snow day'. 60s, plain snowballs only, no building. 10 hits to melt him, you take 3. Specials at 15/30/45s (Blizzard Burst, then Double Blizzard) are instant loss outside a safe zone, with a 2.5s snowflake warning; the two mounds move at each wind-up. Prize: his pot hat on the porch screen.
- Session: up to 3 named streets (Maple Court, Ivy Terrace, The Summit Kids); gear carries across the day, nothing carries into a new snow day.

NEXT: host playtests Frosty and persistent gear; Systems builds the siege and reruns the bot log.

sections.title: Hook: Snow Day (Creative v0)
sections.text:
Chestnut Street against three rival streets, three sledding hills each, and the streetlights are about to come on. Get the toboggan to the crown and hold it there longer than they do.
TONE: cozy = warm, silly, low stakes. Every upgrade is garage or kitchen junk: the launcher is a tennis-ball thrower, the rock is dirty plough ice, the bazooka is a cardboard-tube snow cannon. If it looks like a weapon ad, reskin it.
FIRST 30s: the whistle, sled 2–3m from your porch, everybody sprints. No tutorial; teach by racing.
LIGHT: the sky resets each round because it is the round clock, not the evening's.

sections.title: What a good throw feels like (Creative)
sections.text:
A snowball is a hard flat line (0.35s + 0.05s/m) arriving as the kid flinches; a free, watching kid at 6–10m is hit ≥60%. Reflex-dodging is NOT the skill.
1) The skill is the angle: a kid facing you sees it; one at your side, behind, or busy can't. A 30–45% match hit rate is healthy.
2) A plain ball NEVER clears a wall — walls are the reason to move. Only the blower (0.50s + 0.12s/m) arcs.
3) A miss looks like a near miss: it skids past the boots, ≥80% within 1.2m.

sections.title: Greybox verdict rules (QA) — decide before we look
sections.text:
Three first-timers, no coaching, one greybox match (first to 2 rounds of 120s, hill A, final camera, full dusk ending, porch screen). Temp audio: whistle, crunch, sled shout, release, impact, wall break, lights clunk; no sound for a landing ring. No audio = void session.

WATCH, nothing asked: 1) touches the sled within 20s; 2) hands off in minute 1 (QA #23); 3) builds unprompted in round 1, and whether a cooldown press stops them; 4) says who's winning at 35s and 105s; 5) porch button + hover time (QA #24); 6) what they look at while carrying (QA #25). Log the first unprompted complaint verbatim, with the minute.
STOPWATCH: seconds the human can't act (chilled, walking, at the stand; carrying counts as play). Target <15%; >25% = bench or walk too long.
CSV: human's crown-second share (QA #21); sudden-death rounds (>1 in 6 = scoring too flat); crown vs open-field chills.
AFTER: What told you time was running out (sky or countdown)? How did you know the sled changed hands? Lose sight of sled or kid? What changed the score? Best moment? What did you do when not carrying? Reopen the shop on purpose?

ONE FIX PER FAILURE:
- never touches the sled → cut a rule or move a spawn, never a prompt.
- never hands off → fix the ally wave, no text.
- never builds → cut the human's build; Brick keeps his walls.
- stops building after a cooldown press → bolder ghost footprint, no text.
- can't say who's winning → fix the score strip.
- loses the sled → camera or pennant failed; no new HUD.
- not in the score → move the round 2–3 sled toward Chestnut; never slow allies.
- picks 'Finish snow day' → don't shorten the clock. Bucket possession changes by 30s: mostly in the first 60s = fix crown/geometry; late = the ending failed.

n=3 proves confusion, not fun. Fun verdict = the host playing a whole match.

nodes.title: Snow Day whistle
nodes.notes: Everyone starts on their own porch. Round 1: sled 2–3m from the human's porch (the tutorial), plain snowballs only. Rounds 2–3: sled at the foot of the hill, centre, with whatever the garage sold. Everybody sprints.
nodes.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

nodes.title: Snowball exchange
nodes.notes: Carry the sled to the crown and hold it; the carrier is slow and unarmed, so teammates escort and wall the approach (middle-click). Holding the crown draws a siege volley. Hit = chilled (see Cocoa stand).
nodes.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

nodes.title: Streetlights = round over
nodes.notes: Lights flicker on at 120s: most crown-seconds takes the round. Level = sudden death.
nodes.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

nodes.title: Porch screen → Garage shop
nodes.notes: Only while the match is still open. Porch screen: grudge line + round score, 'Continue'. Then the garage: one purchase per kid (rule 4); upgrades last the match. Then the next hill: yours, theirs, the park.
nodes.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

nodes.title: Sudden death (capped 60s)
nodes.notes: Per ROUND, not per match: if crown-seconds are level at the streetlights, sudden death. First team to hold the crown 5 continuous seconds; after 60s, the first crown-second wins. A match can never end tied.
nodes.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

nodes.title: Match end on the porch
nodes.notes: First team to 2 rounds wins. Porch screen: the grudge line + score, then 'Next street' / 'Finish snow day' (win or lose). After street 3: 'New snow day' / 'Finish snow day'.
nodes.author: claude

nodes.title: Cocoa stand
nodes.notes: Side of the hill. Chilled kid walks over, warms up, jogs back: ~8s total. Out of play while there (not targetable, not counted). A dropped sled stays where it fell.
nodes.author: claude

nodes.title: Frosty wakes up (bonus bout)
nodes.notes: On 'Next street' / 'New snow day' only. 60s, your kid vs Frosty on the crown, plain snowballs only, no building: 10 hits melt him, his normal throws take 1 of your 3. Specials at 15/30/45s (Blizzard Burst, then Double Blizzard) are instant loss outside a safe zone; the two mounds move at each wind-up. Win: pot hat on the porch screen. Lose: nothing.

nodes.title: Snow day ends
nodes.notes: 'Finish snow day' skips Frosty. The porch screen shows the day's grudges and any pot hats won, then back to the title.

entries.label: Scoring
entries.text: 1 pt per second the sled is carried on the crown; most at 120s wins. Credits buy upgrades, never decide a round.
entries.author: user

entries.label: Porch screen: two lines, no stats
entries.text: Line 1 = the grudge, may name one kid ('Maple Court took your hill — Beanie got you twice'). Line 2 = the round score. Between rounds: 'Continue' to the garage; match end adds the street buttons (rule 10). Starting a new snow day shows 'New snow day — yesterday's garage gear has melted.' The only place history, names and Frosty's pot hats appear.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

objects.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems
objects.title: Core loop rules — Systems (numbers kept stable: 2 ruled out, 6b ruled out, 9 dropped with the cards)

entries.label: 1. Sled is carried, not camped
entries.text: Carrier: 60% speed, can't throw or build. No stealing: the sled changes hands only when a chilled carrier drops it in place (anyone may grab it) or by handoff (rule 6). A dropped sled doesn't score. Camping = slow, unarmed target, so teammates escort.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 2. Idle sled slides home
entries.text: Nobody touching the sled for 15s and it slides back to the bottom of the hill (kids shout). Score pauses. Kills the 0-0 turtle and forces someone to be the sucker.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 3. Sudden death
entries.text: Tie at the lights: first team to hold the crown 5 continuous s wins (a drop, chill or rival pickup resets it); after 60s, the first crown-second wins. The cap never pauses.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 4. Garage shop + economy
entries.text:
Between rounds only; every kid shops, bots too. Round 1 of street 1 = plain snowballs.
PERSISTENCE (host): upgrades and unspent credits last the whole snow day, all 3 streets, for every kid including the bots. 'New snow day' wipes everyone back to plain, and the porch screen says so: 'New snow day — yesterday's garage gear has melted.'
CREDITS: 1 per hit, 1 per 6 crown-seconds, 4 per round played, +2 per round win.
PRICES: ice 4, melter 4, rock 8, snowman 8, launcher 10. Ice and rock share the ball slot (buying one swaps out the other).
GUARDS: one purchase per visit. Street tier comes from rule 10; purchases never change it. Spending never touches scoring.
BOT WISHLISTS (first affordable): Beanie ice → launcher → rock; Pockets melter → snowman (keeps the blower); Brick melter → ice; Copycat copies the human's last buy, else ice → launcher.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 5. Builds: snow wall by default
entries.text: Middle-click plants ONE low wall (1.5m) at your feet, facing your aim. 1s plant (busy); planting again moves it. 8s cooldown after any plant or break. Blocks flat throws; ice and rock break it. A bought snowman replaces it (rule 7). Igloo and fort: host-approved, not built yet.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 6b. Free-sled claim — allies never rob the human
entries.text:
Chestnut's three allies never claim a free sled while the HUMAN is the nearest Chestnut kid to it, for the first 4s the sled is free. They don't stop or wait: they run to support (crown, flank, wall) exactly as normal, and Pip still beats you to every loose sled you are not closest to. After 4s free, or the moment you are not nearest, ordinary Beanie logic applies and someone grabs it.

WHY: the round-1 sled sits 2–3m from the porch, so Beanie logic alone decides the first possession before a first-timer's hands are even on the keys — exactly the spectator case QA #21 measures. This is a possession-assignment clause, not bot hesitation: no animation, nothing on screen, fair-bot rule untouched, and rivals are exempt (Maple's Beanie will still sprint at YOUR free sled). Fails safe: if human carry share is still under 1/3, move the sled start, never make the allies slower.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 6. One order = handoff
entries.text: While carrying, left-click shoves the sled to the one outlined ally within 6m (carrier types only, never Brick). Otherwise it does nothing: no toss, cooldown or sound. Teacher: an eligible ally within 6m with no ring on them waves for the sled. No text.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 7. Throwing: aim a spot, hard line
entries.text:
Mouse aims a landing ring (r 0.8m); left-click throws. Ring visible to all from commitment; ball casts a shadow dot. Your ring hides while you carry; the handoff outline replaces it (QA #25).
- Plain: 0.35s + 0.05s/m, flat, 12m, NEVER clears a wall.
- Ice: 0.25s + 0.03s/m, flat, 12m, shatters the wall it hits.
- Rock: plain flight; smashes through walls and snowmen and keeps going; knocks a kid it chills 1.5m off the spot, away from the sled they dropped.
- Launcher: hold to spray: 0.3s + 0.04s/m, 9m, ring 0.45m, scatter ≤0.5m, 15-ball hopper, 2.5s reload. One pellet chills; balance by price and shop gate, not damage.
- Melter: walk into a rival wall/snowman to melt it; touch a chilled teammate to thaw them (once per 6s; host's call, restores 'heal a chilled ally').
- Snowman: replaces your wall (3 hits, 12s cooldown); pelts rivals within 8m every 2.2s.
- Blower (Pockets): 0.50s + 0.12s/m, high lob, clears walls, 14m.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 8. Nothing gets built on the crown
entries.text: No walls inside the 4m crown circle or within 2m of the sled: no camping under cover.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 10. Session ladder — 3 streets; gear carries across the day
entries.text:
Snow day = up to 3 streets (~20 min). Garage upgrades carry across the day's streets (rule 4); nothing carries into a new snow day. Plain rings: Beanie, Copycat; blower cappers: Pockets; Brick never throws.
Street 1 (Maple Court): Beanie, Pockets, Brick, Copycat; siege 2.0s; 2 plain (lead + side) + 1 capper; reaction 0.60s.
Street 2 (Ivy Terrace): same mix and rings; 1.5s; 0.50s.
Street 3 (The Summit Kids): Beanie + 2 Pockets + Brick; 1.45s; 1 plain lead + 2 cappers on both exits; 0.45s.
Cadence floor 1.45s. Never more than 4 live rings (QA #29).
After each match: equal 'Next street' / 'Finish snow day'; after street 3: 'New snow day' / 'Finish snow day'.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 11. Build numbers
entries.text:
Crown = same flat 4m radius on every hill; only approaches change. Greybox reaction 0.50s (log header).
SPEEDS: kid 4.5 m/s, carrier 2.7 m/s, no stamina or slope modifier. No dodge button: a dodge is walking out of a ring (right-click); a 0.8m step from standstill ≈ 0.25s.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: 12. Camera: one fixed iso shot
entries.text: Whole ~26m hill in one 1280×720 frame (~49px/m, kids ~48px). No follow or pan; human, sled, crown, both porches and flanks always visible. Same footprint on all three hills. Each porch at the foot of its side; kids emerge in a 1.2m arc, human front-centre.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: 13. Busy vs free stance
entries.text: BUSY (planting) can't move. A CARRIER walks 2.7 m/s: 1.0m out of a ring in 0.37s, 2.0m in 0.74s. A FREE kid steps 0.8m in ~0.25s. That gap is why the siege bites and the bracket must come from range. The pose is the information.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Equip slots: owning everything must not stack everything (Systems)
entries.text:
With gear persisting, income is ~20 credits a match and the whole shelf is 36, so by street 2–3 every kid owns every item. If ownership stacks, street 3 is eight kids carrying launchers and snowmen: the field breaks QA #29's ≤4 live rings and the 1.2m miss rule, and the shop has no decisions left after half a snow day.
FIX, and it needs no new items (Creative is right not to fill the shelf yet): a kid CARRIES one throw and one build replacement. Ice and rock already share one slot, the snowman already replaces the wall — so make it explicit that owning the launcher does not delete the plain ball, you choose which throw you carry. Swapping is FREE in the garage and uses the same visit, so a street-3 visit becomes 'which two for this hill' (melter or snowman against street 3's two blowers). Your collection persists; your loadout is two of it. That is also Art's owned-vs-equipped distinction, with a slot strip in the garage.
SIEGE IMMUNITY: a siege volley always uses the street's listed rings (rule 10), never a bot's purchased item. Rule 4 already promises rival purchases never change the street tier; this keeps that true and keeps the ≤4 ring cap honest once every bot owns a launcher. Bot gear still counts in the open field, which is where it was bought for.
TEST: log swaps per shop visit on streets 2–3. Zero swaps once items are owned = the late shop is a dead screen, and that is the signal to fill the shelf — not before.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

objects.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa
objects.title: QA: playtest risks — test these before adding anything

entries.label: 15. Outcomes read as aftermath — ACCEPTED
entries.text: Spec in Art 'Feedback'. TEST: unlabelled 60s clip, ask 'how many throws missed?' None = misses aren't rendering; hit vs untouched unclear = chill state too subtle.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 17. Cocoa stand out of play — ACCEPTED
entries.text: TEST: log repeat-chills within 5s of returning; more than a couple = the stand is exposed, move it further off the hill.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 21. Is the human actually in the score?
entries.text: Pip and Scoop can win without the human. CSV: crown-seconds per carrier; share <1/3 is calibration, not a gate. FAIL only if share <1/3 AND they credit only an ally's carry for the score. FIX: move the round 2–3 sled 1.5m toward Chestnut; never slow allies.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 23. Handoff: count silent presses
entries.text: A failed handoff is silent. From the input log, count carrying throw-presses before the first success, per round: 1–2 = the wave taught it; 3+ = fix the wave (ally turns, arm higher), never a ring, number or tooltip; no handoff at all = 'never hands off'.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 24. 'Next street' is the verdict
entries.text: Log the button + hover seconds. Next fast = wants more; hovering Next ~10s then Finish = a cost not worth paying; Finish instantly = done. No prompting; Next never styled nicer than Finish.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 25. Aim ring hidden while carrying — ACCEPTED
entries.text: TEST: ask what they watched while carrying and how they knew where rings would land. Watching their own cursor = the ring is stealing the siege read.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 26. Shop limits — ACCEPTED
entries.text: Between rounds only, one purchase per visit, no unlocks across snow days (rule 4). TEST: does a first-timer reopen the shop unprompted? If not, it's a screen, not a system: cut prices, keep two items.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 28. Shop beginner fix — RULED
entries.text: Cheapest item = 4 = a no-hit, no-crown round (rule 4). Shop screen may use text (host). TEST: ask 'what could you afford?'; counting aloud twice = the screen isn't reading.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 29. Max live rings — RULED: cap 4
entries.text: A volley is held back if it would put >4 siege rings in flight on one carrier. CSV logs max live rings per carrier per round.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 31. Siege vs bench — RULED: one combined number
entries.text: A chill costs ~8s, so <15% allows two chills per round; a willing carrier's 2–3 holds can blow that while the crown works. Report human chills + bench seconds as one number. Bench >15% with holds at 8–20s: cut warm-up 8s → 5s first, move the stand second. Never shorten cadence for a bench number.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 32. Persisting powerups — RULED (host): across the snow day, wiped at 'New snow day'
entries.text: GATE (QA): compare street 2–3 win rate with street 1. A jump of more than ~20 points means growing kits are inverting the ladder. Fix the street tier first (rule 10), not persistence. Also watch for the shelf running dry by street 3; the unbuilt bazooka, igloo and fort can refill it.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 33. The dead garage: owned-everything arrives by street 3
entries.text:
With gear carried across the day, ~20 credits/match against a 34-credit shelf means most kids own everything by street 3, and the street-2/3 garage becomes a modal that asks nothing — the worst kind of screen, because it still costs a click.
TEST (free, from the log): log garage visits per street and, per visit, purchases and swaps. DEAD VISIT (nothing bought or swapped) on more than one visit per match by street 2 = the shop is furniture.
FIX ORDER: 1) a dead visit becomes a free swap, so the garage still asks 'which two for this hill'; 2) only then new items. Do NOT add items before this number exists.
STATUS OF TWO-SLOT LOADOUT: not ruled, and not built. Treat it as the pre-agreed fallback if the street 2–3 win rate jumps >20pt (rule 4), never as a feature to spec now. Melter's slot is unresolved (Art is right), so the loadout can't be specced until someone decides it.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 34. Correction to #24: 'Next' is no longer a clean verdict
entries.text:
Persistence quietly breaks QA #24, our cheapest verdict on whether the game is worth continuing. 'Next street' now also buys you gear for later hills, so a fast Next is partly a value calculation, not just appetite.
READ IT THIS WAY: hover time on Next, streets 1 → 2 → 3. Flat or falling = they want more hills. Rising = they're pricing the button, and Frosty's bout is inheriting the resentment. Do not read the first Next of a session as a verdict; the porch screen is now a shop decision.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: 48px identity — one rig, four variants
entries.text: One rig, four head/coat silhouettes reused by both teams. Priority: head shape, team colour + scarf pattern, pose. Chestnut = burnt orange bands. Rivals by street: Maple Court = deep teal V; Ivy Terrace = plum dots; The Summit Kids = mustard zigzag (Foreman placeholders, Art may swap, but never a colour near orange). White overhead chevron = human only. Busy state from real carry/plant poses, no icon. Pennant on the sled, stays with a dropped sled. Charm goes in snowbanks and porch lights, not 48px detail.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Throw readout
entries.text: Plain: short bright streak, dark underside, moving shadow; never a lob. Blower: raised ball, broken coral touchdown bracket. Preview stops at walls; footprint matches collision. No more warning layers before human testing.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Score strip + ownership
entries.text: Pennant = carrier's team; dropped = white. Crown edge pulses each scoring second. Top strip: teams, crown-seconds, sled icon by the scorer, exact countdown in the last 20s; dusk and lamps reinforce it. Handoff preview outlines ONE eligible ally within 6m with a short sled arrow; never Brick.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Greybox readability gate (human eyes, not telemetry)
entries.text:
Hill A, 1280×720, three unlabelled 1s clips (8-kid scrum / lob / wall interception) at sunset and dusk. A first-timer names human, carrier, leading team and incoming threat, then points to an escape; record errors and time.
FLANK: from each porch they point at the flank route within 1s, at dusk too.
MEASURE: kids ≥48px; landing footprint in projection; misses ≤1.2m for ≥80% (world-space CSV). The capture beats arithmetic.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Feedback: aftermath + wall status
entries.text:
HIT: chilled, stopped kid + brief puff. MISS: ball resting at the end of its skid. WALL BLOCK: lasting dent, not a hole; only ice/rock break walls. Never hide chevron or pennant; no clouds or screen shake.
WALL STATUS: ghost footprint fills with the cooldown, full outline when ready, barred when illegal; never looks solid. The plant pose starts only on a legal plant.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: New-day reset notice — before commitment
entries.text: Beside 'New snow day', before the click: 'Fresh snow, fresh start — your gear and credits reset.' Keep visible, not hover-only; no extra confirmation modal. Next street never shows reset copy. At Frosty entry, a short 'Snowballs only — your gear returns next street' explains temporary kit removal. Avoid 'gear melted': launcher and other garage junk don't melt.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

objects.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative
objects.title: The eight kids — AI as characters

entries.label: Beanie — always wants the sled
entries.text: Makes the crown a door anyone can kick open. Silhouette: striped beanie.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Pockets — keeps 6m away (leaf blower)
entries.text: Back-line lobber; teaches you to respect the landing ring. Silhouette: bulging pockets.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Brick — only builds
entries.text: Walls the approach so his team's carry is easy. Silent, calm, faintly comic. Silhouette: too-big mittens, sits low.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Copycat — copies your action, never your allegiance
entries.text: Mirrors your last action type, exaggerating your throw pose. Wears his own street's colours and his own hat: head shape is the top identity cue, so he never borrows yours.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Chestnut's three — your street
entries.text: Pip (Beanie logic), Scoop (Pockets), Waffle (Brick). Same rig, orange bands, no new mechanics.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Names, not dialogue
entries.text: Learned by behaviour; names appear only in the porch grudge line. No barks or text in flow: cozy = quiet.
entries.author: agent:~deepseek/deepseek-flash-latest=creative

entries.label: Behaviour rules (Systems) — no state trees
entries.text:
Beanie: grabs a free sled, shortest legal path to the crown. Throws only when the sled has been off the crown 5s+. Never builds.
Pockets: blower only; holds 6–10m from the nearest enemy, faces their carrier, backs off inside 6m. Carries only as fallback.
Brick: never carries, receives or throws. Keeps his wall between his carrier and the nearest threat (outside the crown, ≥2m from the sled); wall down = walks 2m ahead as a shield.
Copycat: 2s after the human acts, repeats that action type; never initiates (copies the stand-in in bot runs).
SIEGE suspends Beanie's 5s rule and Copycat's never-initiate rule, for volley throws only (Host playtest 1).
FAIR-BOT: reacts only to committed rings in its ~120° front arc, after its reaction time, by walking 0.8m out (rule 11). Carriers and builders don't dodge.
Difficulty = street tier (rule 10); reaction 0.45–0.60s governs dodging only. Fallback carrier when Beanie is chilled 3s+: Pockets, then Copycat.
ALLIES: same logic. They never take a handoff the human didn't give, but a sled the human drops is free for anyone (6b stays ruled out).
SHOPPING: wishlists in rule 4.
STAND-IN (bot runs): Beanie logic, plain snowballs; in shop tests buys the item under test.

objects.title: Greybox bot round — logs and pass/fail (Systems)

entries.label: Record one CSV, one fixed seed
entries.text:
Per second: sled state, both scores. Per throw: thrower, item, distance, ring position, flight time, outcome (hit / wall / empty / stepped out), target facing and busy. Per volley: shared release-frame ID (verifies one release per cadence). Per miss: closest approach. Per kid: chills, credits, purchases. Per round, 30s buckets: possession changes and handoffs, separately.
Conditions: hill A, stand-in in the human slot, bots shopped to their street tier. Run at the tier being gated: the siege gate uses street 1 (0.60s); other checks use 0.50s.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Pass/fail — does the loop exist
entries.text: Sled on the crown 25–60% of the round; ≥6 possession changes per round; longest hold ≤25s, else camping: fix geometry or a rule, never HUD. Log siege volleys (count, rings, hits).
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Pass/fail — are the decisions real
entries.text:
Clear a ring = reaction + 0.25s step + 0.1s slop (0.95 / 0.85 / 0.80s by street).
Free, facing kid at 6–10m: hit ≥60% (<50% = flight time wrong). Busy or flanked: ~100%.
Match hit rate 30–45%: >60% = bots blind; <25% = no flank route, fix geometry.
Chills: 4–8 per team per round, ≤2 per kid (2 × 8s = 13% of 120s); a 3rd is a geometry/spawn report. Count crown-hold chills apart from open-field.
Misses: ≥80% within 1.2m; a ball through a body is a collision bug.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Shop phase: per-item win rate, one retune then delete
entries.text: Per item: 30+ matches (0.50s, hill A) with the stand-in forced to buy it, vs plain-snowball control on the same seeds. Outside 40–60% win rate: one retune (price first), then cut. Launcher is the first suspect.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=systems

entries.label: Wall-block share
entries.text: Share of plain throws that die on a wall. <25%: ship. 25–35%: watch, shorten the flank. >35%: walls are the game; fix geometry (wider flank) or a slower rebuild, not a new card.

objects.author: claude
objects.title: Host playtest 1: the crown is too safe (Systems, implement)

entries.label: Diagnosis (from greybox/src/sim/ai.ts)
entries.text: Vs a human on the crown only Pockets attacked (one blower per 8s, easy to walk out of). Beanie waits for a drop, Copycat mirrors throws a carrier can't make, Brick never throws: 3 of 4 rivals passive exactly when the human scores.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Fix 1: Siege — one shared volley, not per-bot cadences
entries.text:
TRIGGER: an enemy carries the sled within 2m of the crown edge; ends when the sled is dropped, carried 2m+ away, or retaken by the defenders.
Every free defender (not chilled, carrying or planting) joins ONE shared volley timer, so each volley is one visible event. AI exceptions are in the behaviour rules; Brick still never throws.
SYMMETRIC: Pip/Scoop/Waffle siege a rival carrier the same way, so escorting matters both ways.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Fix 2: Bracket — lead from range, direct shot up close
entries.text:
One volley = every free thrower's ring on the SAME frame (per-street rings in rule 10).
FAR (8m+) plain: lead = carrier position + velocity × flight time; a second ring 1.2m to one side.
NEAR (<8m): one direct shot at the carrier, no lead.
CAPPERS (blowers) land ~1s late on the obvious exit; street 3's two cover both exits.
Bracket punishes running straight, near shot punishes standing still, capper punishes the obvious exit: irregular walking is the skill. Stepping out of a ring inside the 4m crown keeps you scoring. Handoff is the free escape: the volley lands where the sled was. All rings visible from release, no homing.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Gate (don't overcorrect)
entries.text:
Loop gates still hold. NEW: a willing carrier's median street-1 crown hold is 8–20s (≥12 holds over 6 rounds); no carrier chilled by two volleys in a row more than twice per round. Log thrower distance on every siege ring: most crown chills from <8m = near-range rule not implemented.
Never survives 8s → lengthen the volley period. Crown never held → fix geometry (cover outside the crown or a 2m no-throw band). Holds past 20s → add a capper before shortening cadence.
RETUNE one lever at a time: capper count → cadence (1.45–2.0s) → lateral spacing (1.2m). Never shrink the 0.8m ring.
entries.author: claude

objects.author: claude
objects.title: Boss bout: Frosty (merged spec, Foreman + Systems + QA)

entries.label: Frosty: 60s, 10 hits to melt, you can take 3 (host)
entries.text: Your kid alone against Frosty on the same hill, 60s, streetlights on. Frosty sits on the crown, never moves or dodges, and is big and easy to hit. He needs 10 hits to melt; you go down after 3. A hit on you = knockback + cancelled throw, never the cocoa stand. His 3rd hit on you, or the clock, ends it. PLAIN SNOWBALLS ONLY, NO BUILDING: the bout is a pure skill test, so your garage gear stays in the garage (the launcher would erase his 10 hits, and your own wall would bypass the moving mounds). Your gear is still yours on the next street.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Specials: Blizzard Burst, then Double Blizzard (RULED)
entries.text:
NORMAL: aimed volleys at you (lead ring + direct ring + lob); a hit = one of your 3. They pause for the whole special.
SPECIAL 1, BLIZZARD BURST: gapless ring of flat snowballs in every direction; instant loss unless you're in a drawn safe zone (host).
SPECIAL 2, DOUBLE BLIZZARD (from 5 hits left): ONE relocation, ONE warning, then two bursts ~1.5s apart from the same cover (QA's cut). The first demands 'run now', the second 'stay put'; stepping out between them to steal a throw is the greed trap. Renamed from 'Whiteout' so nobody builds a white screen.
WARNING: 2.5s snowflake swirl tight around Frosty, bigger and louder each half-second, a different pose per special. Nothing fires without the full swirl.
SCHEDULE: specials at 15s, 30s and 45s, so 3 per bout. 2s dizzy after each (free throws).
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Shelter moves when he winds up (host) — RULED timing
entries.text:
Two snow mounds. Each special starts with a 0.5s mitten sweep (Creative): the old mounds sink and snow puffs mark exactly where the new ones rise (QA: show the destination first). The new mounds are fully formed BEFORE the 2.5s swirl begins (Art), then locked for the whole warning; nothing ever moves under you mid-warning or mid-impact.
Placement is random, but one mound is always 5–7m from your kid (QA: narrowed from 5–9m so the run always fits; deaths only come from throws you chose to start after the swirl).
The safe zone behind each mound is drawn in the snow. Between specials the mounds stay put. His lob clears them and your plain ball can't, so cover and firing position are opposite sides of the same mound (Systems' trade).
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Prize: Frosty's pot hat on the porch screen (RULED)
entries.text: Win: the porch screen shows Frosty's pot hat beside your street's name for the rest of the snow day, plus the line 'You melted Frosty'. Up to 3 hats in a full snow day. Nothing on the field: history lives only on the porch screen, and a field snowman would read as the bought snowman turret. After street 3 the hat shows on the porch screen before the new snow day starts clean. No power or credits: the bout is a bonus, so its prize never touches balance.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Losing costs nothing
entries.text: Getting caught by a special (or taking his 3rd hit) leaves a kid-shaped snowdrift with your hat, then a mitten, popping out (Creative). Win: Frosty slumps into a heap with his pot on top. No credits or items lost; the bout is a bonus, never a tax.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Placement: 'Next street' plays it, 'Finish' skips it
entries.text: The bout sits after the porch screen (QA), so it never delays the Next/Finish read (#24). 'Next street' or 'New snow day' plays the bout, then the next whistle; 'Finish snow day' skips it. No third button. WATCH: if players who chose Next still quit during the bout, shorten it before adding anything.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Art fairness gate — a full warning starts at readable cover
entries.text: The burst's collision is gapless at the farthest playable radius and matches the visible snow; the drawn safe zone equals the real blocked area. TEST at 720p, frozen on the frame the old mound sinks: within 0.5s, a first-timer points at where the new safe side will be (QA), then reaches it with right-click before release from the worst legal spot.
entries.author: agent:openai/gpt-6.1-sol=new-role

entries.label: Hold the boss art until the base loop passes one gate
entries.text:
No siege in the prototype, no bot log, no human match since the host's complaint. The bout now has 13 entries, two concept sheets, a new HUD that replaces the score strip and a death animation.

RULE: no boss art, no boss HUD, no bout code until the siege log passes (median crown hold 8–20s over ≥12 holds). A 60s boss standing on the same hill inherits whatever is wrong with the crown, and with one witness instead of eight it will look like it works.
entries.author: agent:deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017=qa

entries.label: Tuning + what to log (RULED)
entries.text:
BUDGET: 3 specials. A Blizzard Burst costs ~5.5s of no normal throwing (0.5 sweep + 2.5 warning + release + 2 dizzy); a Double Blizzard ~7s. That's ~18s, leaving ~42s of normal-phase throwing plus ~6s of dizzy windows. At about 1 hit per 2.5s while under fire, 10 hits fits for a player who throws in the open, spending 1–2 of their 3 hit points. That's a skilled-player fit, not a guaranteed win.
RED LINES: median 1–2 hit points spent. 0 in most bouts = open throws are free: strengthen the normal volley. Most bouts end at 3 hits taken = too harsh: lengthen the gap between specials. First-timers median under 8 hits landed at the buzzer = too tight: drop to 2 specials (at 20s and 40s) to give back ~5s of throwing. Changing the 10 is the host's call; never the 2.5s warning or the 60s clock.
LOG: hits landed by second; hits taken split normal/special; seconds from swirl start to reaching a safe zone; the throw gap across each special.
entries.author: claude

entries.label: Bout kit: an owned launcher goes silent — show it before they press
entries.text:
The bout takes the launcher you just bought and makes it silent, three times over a snow day. A returning player presses left-click, sees a plain ball, and reads it as broken — not as a challenge.
FIX (no new rule): the first second of the bout shows a plain snowball in the kid's hand and the build ghost is absent, not greyed. Same language as 'barred, never looks solid'.
TEST: in the bot/human log of bout rounds 2–3, count throw-presses in the first 2s that produce no ball, and any player who presses middle-click at all. More than a stray press = the kit you own isn't visibly gone.
